ἀφροσύναι· διὰ ταύτας γὰρ καὶ ἀκάρδιος γεγονὼς, κτήσασθαι σοφίαν ἀδυνα τεῖ. –Ἐν
παντὶ πράγματι, πᾶς ὁ ὑψῶν ἑαυτὸν τα πεινωθήσεται· ὅτι Κύριος ὑπερηφάνοις
ἀντιτάσσεται· ὁ δὲ σκολιάζων τοῦ μαθεῖν τὰ πράγματα τοῦ Θεοῦ, ἐμπεσεῖται εἰς κακὰ
περὶ τὴν κρίσιν. Ἐνταῦθα φίλον τὸν Χριστόν φησιν, ὃς διὰ τὴν πρὸς ἄνθρωπον
φιλίαν, ἄνθρωπος γέγονεν. Οὐκέτι γὰρ λέγω ὑμᾶς δούλους, εἶπεν τοῖς μαθηταῖς,
ἀλλὰ φίλους· ἐν παντὶ δὲ καιρῷ ὁ Χριστὸς συνυπαρχέτω σοι φίλος εἰ δὲ οἱ τοῦ
Χριστοῦ υἱοὶ, ἀλλήλων εἰσὶ φίλοι· οἱ ἄγ γελοι καὶ οἱ δίκαιοι ἄνθρωποι, ἀλλήλων
εἰσὶν ἀδελ 17.201 φοὶ, τῷ τῆς υἱοθεσίας γεννώμενοι πνεύματι· τούτου γὰρ χάριν καὶ
γεννῶνται ὑπὸ τῆς σοφίας, ἵνα ἀνθρώ πους ὁδηγήσωσιν ἀπὸ κακίας εἰς ἀρετὴν, καὶ
ἀπὸ ἀγνωσίας εἰς ἐπίγνωσιν Θεοῦ. Οὗτός ἐστιν εὐμετάβολος, ὁ ῥᾳδίως ἀπὸ ἀρετῆς
ἐπὶ κακίαν μεταβαλλόμενος, τοῖς πονηροῖς λογισμοῖς συν απαχθείς. Πατέρα ἐνταῦθα
τὸν Θεόν φησι· μητέρα, τὴν φι λανθρωπί
pass_a_gloss: Foolishness blocks wisdom; pride leads to humiliation; distorting divine truth brings judgment. Christ, loving humanity, became human and called disciples friends, not servants, abiding with them always. Those who are Christ’s children are mutual friends; the meek and just are brothers, born of adoption’s Spirit, begotten by wisdom to lead from evil to good, from ignorance to knowing God. The fickle easily fall from virtue to vice, swayed by bad thoughts. God is Father; His love for humanity is Mother, who bore Him in flesh and let Him suffer for us. God Father does not rejoice over an adopted son untaught in divine wisdom, but over one who gives himself to evil. A wise son gladdens his mother, God’s love, which brings us to God as weaned ones craving spiritual food, so that as God’s Son Jesus became our brother by likeness, we live accordingly in act and speech. Our mother is the Church, joined to God by the Holy Spirit as wife, ever bearing His sons and daughters. She rejoices over those taught in God’s wisdom and knowledge, Father and Church alike; but mourns deeply for the untaught, as though we refuse to return and be saved. Not to remain in evil but to persist in wickedness. Here the visage of contemplation is declared: contemplation indeed is the intellect of a wise man, wisdom, knowledge, and justice; yet the discerning eyes of the senseless, and within the flesh in the peak of iniquity and malignity. Divine wrath upon the foolish son from God and Father is dispatched on the day of reckoning; but to the Church birthed by the Spirit, and to the assembly of the saints, sorrow shall assuredly be at the ruin of the foolish son; and since the prudent son possesses both progenitor and dam, the witless has sole progenitor; for dam and progenitor are identical, yet progenitor is not invariably dam; for should the offspring perish in vice and unawareness, the progenitor endures, but dam does not—inasmuch as the offspring has not shared in the Spirit of filial adoption; thus too concerning carnal mothers it shall be reasoned, and regarding the demise of the fleshly: we shall name dam and progenitor, but no longer dam of the deceased offspring. One errs by depriving the just of his due, or by twisting his pupils toward wrongdoing, and transgresses; for holding them in dominion, he has been harmed; for they pursue not our possessions, but us; and he terms mighty those who rule in Christ. The one driven by demonic folly lacks want of divine wisdom or insight; for he has preferred gloom over radiance; and even if he exults in folly, he imagines himself devoid of need for wisdom. As water vivifies flora, so the discourse of a man grounded in virtue revives the excellences, and wings toward the Deity those desiring sagacity; and he depicts a river springing upward, the unspeakable bounty of the Spirit’s sanctified wisdom, the perpetual flow of wisdom from the thrice-holy essence. The one accepting and enacting the devil’s inherent wickedness, operating thereby in speculation and utterance, whose subjects he marvels at as the countenance of the ungodly; yet the equitable in adjudication, and in discourse concerning corporeal forms, it is not commendable to spurn the sacred.
pass_b_english:
Foolishness: for by these things one becomes heartless and unable to acquire wisdom. In every matter, whoever exalts himself will be humbled, for the Lord opposes the proud. And the one who twists the learning of God’s things will fall into evil concerning judgment. Here he speaks of the beloved Christ, who, because of his love for humanity, became human. No longer do I call you servants, he said to the disciples, but friends. And in every season, may Christ abide with you as a friend. But if those who are children of Christ are mutually friends, then the gentle and the righteous are also brothers to one another, being born of the Spirit of adoption. For this reason they are begotten by wisdom, so that they may lead people from wickedness to virtue and from ignorance to the knowledge of God. This is the fickle person, easily turned from virtue to wickedness, yielding to evil reasonings. Here he calls God Father, and his love for humanity Mother, who has begotten him in the flesh and made him endure suffering for our sake. But our God and Father does not rejoice over a son adopted yet untaught in God’s wisdom and knowledge, but rather over one who abandons himself to wickedness and malice. However, a wise son brings joy to his mother, the love of God, who draws us to God and the Father as weaned sons, longing for the spiritual, solid nourishment, so that just as the Son of God, Jesus Christ, has become our brother by likeness, we too may conduct ourselves in deed and word. Moreover, our mother is the Church, whom God and the Father have joined to himself by the Holy Spirit as a wife; for she continually bears sons and daughters for him. And indeed, over those who are being instructed in God’s knowledge and wisdom, both our Father God and the Mother Church rejoice; but over the uninstructed, she deeply grieves and sorrows, as if we were unwilling to turn back and be saved.

But rather to persist in wickedness. Here the face of contemplation is spoken of: for contemplation is the understanding of an intelligent man, wisdom and knowledge and righteousness; but the intellectual eyes of the foolish, and within the body in the extremity of wickedness and depravity. Wrath is sent forth against the foolish son by God and the Father on the day of judgment; but to the Church which has begotten by the Spirit, and to the choir of the holy, grief will certainly be upon the destruction of the foolish son; and that whereas the wise son has both begetter and mother, the foolish has only the begetter; for the mother and the begetter are one, but the begetter is not always also a mother; for if the begotten perishes in wickedness and ignorance, the begetter remains, but the mother does not; because even the begotten has not partaken of the Spirit of adoption; likewise also concerning sensible mothers it will be thought, and concerning the death of the sensible: we shall call the mother and the begetter, but no longer the mother of the dead child. One transgresses by taking away the righteous man’s due, or by perverting his disciples toward injustice, and sins; for having possession of them, he has suffered loss; for they do not seek our things, but us; and he calls powerful those who reign in Christ. The one led by the foolishness of demons has no need of God’s wisdom or knowledge; for he has loved darkness more than light; and even if he rejoices in foolishness, he thinks he needs no wisdom. As water makes plants grow, so the word of a man established in virtues refreshes the virtues, and bears aloft toward God those who wish to become wise; and he speaks of a river leaping forth, the ineffable grace of the wisdom of the all-holy Spirit, the ever-flowing wisdom of the triune divine unity. The one who receives and acts upon the existing wickedness of the devil, in contemplation and speech, whose persons he admires as the face of the impious; but the just in judgment, and in word concerning bodies, it is not good to reject the holy.
